title: Launchpad Complete Guide
subtitle: Master Token Launches from IDOs to Fair Launch Mechanisms

intro.title: Introduction to Token Launches
intro.content:
Token launches are how new crypto projects enter the market and distribute their tokens to early supporters. Unlike traditional IPOs that require regulatory approval and are limited to accredited investors, crypto token launches are globally accessible and come in many forms—from centralized IDOs to completely permissionless fair launches.

In this comprehensive guide, you'll learn the different launch mechanisms, how to participate safely, and most importantly—how to evaluate projects to avoid scams and rug pulls. We'll cover real examples of successful launches, examine tokenomics structures, and provide a framework for due diligence.

launch_types.title: Types of Token Launches
launch_types.content: Understanding the different launch mechanisms is crucial for both participation and risk assessment. Each type has unique characteristics, advantages, and risks.

ico_history.title: ICO: The Original Token Sale
ico_history.content:
Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs) dominated the 2017 bull market. Projects would publish a whitepaper and accept ETH directly to a contract address in exchange for tokens.

The 2017 ICO Boom: Ethereum raised $18 million in its 2014 ICO. By 2017, projects were raising hundreds of millions. EOS raised $4.1 billion over a year-long ICO. The market was largely unregulated and accessible to anyone.

Why ICOs Declined:

  • Regulatory crackdowns (SEC classified many as securities)
  • Extremely high scam rate (estimated 80%+ of ICOs were scams or failed)
  • No price discovery mechanism—tokens often dumped immediately after listing
  • Lack of vetting—anyone could launch without oversight

Today, traditional ICOs are rare, replaced by more sophisticated mechanisms with better price discovery and vetting.

ido.title: IDO: Decentralized Launches
ido.content:
Initial DEX Offerings (IDOs) launch tokens directly on decentralized exchanges, providing immediate liquidity and trading. Unlike ICOs where you wait weeks or months for exchange listings, IDO tokens are tradeable immediately.

How IDOs Work:

  1. Project partners with a launchpad platform
  2. Launchpad vets the project (due diligence, smart contract audit)
  3. Users stake the launchpad's native token to participate
  4. Allocation is based on tier (how much you stake) and/or lottery
  5. Tokens launch directly into a DEX liquidity pool

Advantages:

  • Immediate liquidity and price discovery
  • Some level of vetting by the launchpad
  • Transparent on-chain process
  • Global accessibility (with some KYC exceptions)

Disadvantages:

  • High competition—popular launches sell out in seconds
  • Must hold launchpad tokens (opportunity cost)
  • Still significant scam risk despite vetting
  • Price can dump hard if tokenomics are poor

ieo.title: IEO: Exchange-Backed Launches
ieo.content:
Initial Exchange Offerings (IEOs) are token sales conducted on centralized exchanges like Binance Launchpad, where the exchange provides vetting, marketing, and immediate listing.

How IEOs Work:

  1. Exchange vets and selects the project
  2. Users buy tokens using the exchange's native token (e.g., BNB for Binance)
  3. Allocation based on holdings or lottery system
  4. Token immediately lists on the exchange

Historical Performance: Early Binance Launchpad projects had extraordinary returns—Matic (Polygon) did 10x within weeks, Elrond did 20x. However, later launches became less profitable as competition increased.

Pros:

  • Strongest vetting (exchanges stake their reputation)
  • Guaranteed listing on major exchange
  • High marketing exposure

Cons:

  • Extremely competitive (millions competing for allocations)
  • Must hold exchange tokens
  • Centralized process (can exclude certain countries)
  • Returns have diminished over time

fair_launch.title: Fair Launch: No Presale, Equal Access
fair_launch.content:
Fair launches have no presale, no team allocation at launch, and no privileged early access. Everyone can participate from day one at the same price.

The Philosophy: Fair launches emerged as a reaction to ICO/IDO scams where teams dump massive pre-allocated tokens on retail buyers. In a fair launch, even the team must buy or earn tokens like everyone else.

Common Fair Launch Mechanisms:

  • Bonding Curves (Pump.fun): Price increases algorithmically as more tokens are bought. Early buyers get better prices, but there's no presale lockup
  • Liquidity Bootstrapping Pools (Fjord): Start at high price and gradually decrease, discouraging bots and whales
  • Pure Fair Launch: All tokens enter a DEX pool at the same time, no vesting

Example: Yearn Finance (YFI) Fair launched in July 2020 with no presale, no team allocation, no VC investors. All 30,000 tokens were distributed to liquidity providers. Within weeks, YFI went from $0 to $40,000. The founder kept only what he personally farmed.

Risks:

  • No vesting means team can sell anytime
  • Susceptible to sniper bots if not properly designed
  • Whales can dominate supply
  • Still no guarantee of legitimacy or success

lbp.title: LBP: Liquidity Bootstrapping Pools
lbp.content:
Liquidity Bootstrapping Pools are a type of fair launch mechanism originally created by Balancer, now primarily offered through Fjord Foundry. They provide superior price discovery compared to traditional launches.

How LBPs Work:

  1. Pool starts with high token weight (e.g., 95% project token, 5% USDC)
  2. Initial price is very high (designed to be unattractive)
  3. Weights gradually shift (e.g., to 50/50 over 3 days)
  4. Price naturally decreases unless there's buying pressure
  5. Final price represents true market demand

Why This Works: The declining price curve discourages bots and FOMO buying. Patient buyers wait for the price to stabilize, while the market finds true demand. This is far more efficient than fixed-price sales where bots fight to buy and immediately dump.

Example Mechanics:

  • Day 1: Token price starts at $10 (too expensive for most)
  • Day 2: Price curve drops to $2 even without selling pressure
  • Day 3: Market buys in, stabilizing at $1.20
  • Result: Fair price discovery, less volatility post-launch

Advantages:

  • Discourages bot manipulation
  • True price discovery
  • Reduces immediate dumps
  • More capital efficient for projects

major_launchpads.title: Major Launchpad Platforms
major_launchpads.content: Different launchpads serve different niches—some focus on high-quality, vetted projects, while others prioritize permissionless access. Understanding each platform's model helps you choose where to participate.

dao_maker.title: DAO Maker: Strong Holder Offering
dao_maker.content:
DAO Maker pioneered the Strong Holder Offering (SHO) model, designed to reward long-term token holders and filter out short-term speculators.

How SHO Works:

  1. Stake DAO tokens to enter
  2. Allocation based on stake amount and duration
  3. Vesting releases tokens gradually over 6-12 months
  4. Can claim vested tokens anytime or stake for extra rewards

The Vetting Process: DAO Maker claims to conduct extensive due diligence—team background checks, product validation, tokenomics review, and legal compliance. However, they still had notable failures (like My Neighbor Alice's poor post-launch performance).

Track Record: Mixed. Early launches like Orion Protocol (ORN) did 20x. Later launches often failed to maintain value. The platform pivoted to offer different allocation tiers and models.

Requirements:

  • Minimum stake varies by tier (typically 500-5000 DAO)
  • KYC required for most sales
  • Some sales restricted by geography

seedify.title: Seedify: Tiered Allocation System
seedify.content:
Seedify uses a nine-tier system where your allocation increases with your SFUND token holdings. They focus on gaming, metaverse, and NFT projects.

Tier Structure:

  • Tier 1-3: Lottery-based allocation (hold minimum SFUND)
  • Tier 4-6: Guaranteed allocation increases with holdings
  • Tier 7-9: Large guaranteed allocations (requires significant SFUND stake)

Example: A Tier 7 holder might get a $2,000 guaranteed allocation, while Tier 2 enters a lottery for potential $100 allocation.

Vetting Focus: Strong emphasis on GameFi projects. They evaluate game development progress, team experience in gaming, and business model viability.

Pros:

  • Clear tier system (know your allocation)
  • Focus on gaming/metaverse niche
  • Incubation services for projects

Cons:

  • High SFUND cost for meaningful allocation
  • GameFi sector volatility
  • Token price dependent on gaming trends

polkastarter.title: Polkastarter: Multi-Chain Launches
polkastarter.content:
Polkastarter is one of the oldest IDO platforms, supporting launches across multiple chains. Originally focused on Polkadot ecosystem, now multi-chain.

Allocation Method:

  1. Stake POLS tokens
  2. Apply for whitelist (varies by project)
  3. If whitelisted, participate in lottery or guaranteed allocation
  4. Some launches use FCFS (first come, first served)

Notable Launches:

  • Covalent (CQT): Blockchain data indexing—successful launch, still operating
  • Quickswap (QUICK): Polygon DEX—major success story
  • Ultra (UOS): Gaming platform—mixed results

Unique Features:

  • Insurance fund for some launches (if project rugs, partial compensation)
  • Multi-chain support (not locked to one ecosystem)
  • Both fixed-price and dynamic pricing options

Challenges:

  • Whitelist process can be opaque
  • Competition remains very high
  • Insurance fund has limited coverage

fjord.title: Fjord Foundry: Fair Price Discovery
fjord.content:
Fjord Foundry (formerly Copper Launch) specializes in Liquidity Bootstrapping Pools, providing the most sophisticated price discovery mechanism in crypto.

How It Works:

  1. Project sets up LBP with starting weights (e.g., 95/5)
  2. Pool duration typically 2-4 days
  3. Weights gradually shift to final ratio (e.g., 50/50)
  4. Anyone can participate—no staking required
  5. Final pool becomes initial DEX liquidity

Example: Alchemix (ALCH) Launched via Copper LBP in Feb 2021. Started at extremely high price, gradually declined until market found fair value around $800. Token maintained value better than most fixed-price launches.

Why Projects Choose LBP:

  • Better price discovery than fixed-price sales
  • Less susceptible to bot manipulation
  • Immediate liquidity post-launch
  • More capital efficient (need less starting capital)

User Benefits:

  • No need to stake platform tokens
  • Can buy at any point during launch period
  • Market-driven pricing reduces FOMO
  • Transparent mechanics

pump_fun.title: Pump.fun: Permissionless Bonding Curve
pump_fun.content:
Pump.fun democratized token launches on Solana with a completely permissionless, bonding curve model. Anyone can launch a token in seconds with zero upfront cost.

The Bonding Curve Model:

  1. Anyone creates a token—no approval needed
  2. Price starts at near-zero and increases algorithmically as tokens are bought
  3. All purchases and sales happen on the bonding curve (no external DEX)
  4. When a threshold market cap is reached (~$69k), liquidity moves to Raydium DEX
  5. Curve is destroyed, token trades freely on Raydium

Formula: The curve typically uses price = k × supply^2, meaning each token costs progressively more than the last.

Phenomenon: Pump.fun became one of Solana's top fee generators, processing thousands of launches daily. Most tokens die quickly (rug pulls or lack of interest), but some achieve massive success.

Success Stories:

  • Bonk-style memecoins launching to multi-million market caps
  • Community tokens gaining traction organically
  • NFT projects using it for fair token distribution

Risks:

  • Extremely high scam rate (90%+ of launches fail/rug)
  • No vetting whatsoever
  • Bonding curve mechanics favor very early buyers
  • Most volume is from degenerate speculation

Use Case: Best for experimental, community-driven projects where fairness and permissionless access matter more than vetting. Not suitable for serious investment.

participation_guide.title: How to Participate in Token Launches
participation_guide.content: Successfully participating in launches requires preparation, understanding platform mechanics, and quick execution. Here's how to navigate the process.

requirements.title: Common Requirements
requirements.content:
Token Holdings: Most launchpads require staking their native token:

  • DAO Maker: 500-5000+ DAO tokens ($500-5000+)
  • Seedify: 50-10,000+ SFUND tokens (varies greatly by tier)
  • Polkastarter: 250+ POLS tokens
  • Fjord/Pump.fun: No platform token required

KYC/AML: Many platforms require identity verification:

  • Passport or government ID
  • Proof of residence
  • Facial verification
  • Processing time: 24 hours to 1 week

Geographic Restrictions: Common exclusions:

  • United States (SEC regulations)
  • China, Iran, North Korea (sanctions)
  • Sometimes: UK, Canada, Singapore (varies by project)

Preparation Checklist:

  1. Complete KYC early (don't wait until launch day)
  2. Acquire and stake platform tokens weeks in advance
  3. Set up wallet with sufficient gas funds
  4. Join project's Discord/Telegram for announcements
  5. Read the whitepaper and tokenomics
  6. Check launch time in your timezone

allocation.title: Understanding Allocation Systems
allocation.content:
Guaranteed Allocation: Higher tiers get fixed allocation amounts. Example on Seedify Tier 8: $3,000 guaranteed allocation regardless of demand.

Lottery Systems: Lower tiers enter a random draw. If selected, you get an allocation. If not, you get nothing. Typical odds: 10-30% depending on oversubscription.

First Come, First Served (FCFS): After guaranteed and lottery rounds, remaining tokens sold to anyone—fastest wins. Requires:

  • Fast internet connection
  • Wallet already connected
  • Transaction pre-signed if possible
  • High gas fees to front-run others

Oversubscription: When demand exceeds supply, allocations are reduced proportionally.

Example:

  • Total raise: $500,000
  • Total demand from qualified users: $2,000,000
  • Oversubscription: 4x
  • If you qualified for $1,000, you get $250

Pro Tip: Read the announcement carefully—some launches use hybrid models (guaranteed + lottery + FCFS rounds). Each round may have different requirements.

kyc.title: KYC and Compliance
kyc.content:
Why KYC Exists:

  • Regulatory compliance (especially for team-based launches)
  • Preventing bots and sybil attacks
  • Geographic restrictions
  • Anti-money laundering requirements

What Information Is Collected:

  • Full legal name
  • Date of birth
  • Residential address
  • Government ID (passport, driver's license)
  • Selfie for facial verification
  • Sometimes: proof of address (utility bill)

Common KYC Providers:

  • Blockpass: Used by many launchpads, reusable across platforms
  • Synaps: Quick verification, mobile-friendly
  • Jumio: Established provider, thorough checks

Privacy Concerns:

  • Your data is stored by third-party providers
  • Data breaches have occurred in the past
  • Information may be shared with authorities
  • Consider: Is the potential allocation worth the privacy trade-off?

KYC-Free Alternatives:

  • Pump.fun, Fjord Foundry (no KYC for participation)
  • Pure fair launches on DEXs
  • Some community launches

Important: Never complete KYC for unknown or unvetted platforms. Scammers create fake launchpads to harvest identity documents.

token_vesting.title: Understanding Token Vesting
token_vesting.content: Vesting schedules determine when and how tokens are released. Understanding these is crucial for evaluating launch viability and price action predictions.

cliff.title: Cliff Periods
cliff.content:
What is a Cliff? A cliff is an initial lockup period where zero tokens are released. After the cliff ends, vesting begins.

Example:

  • 6-month cliff, then 18-month linear vesting
  • Month 0-6: No tokens released
  • Month 6: Cliff ends, first vested batch unlocked
  • Month 6-24: Tokens release gradually each month

Why Cliffs Exist:

  • Aligns team incentives with long-term success
  • Prevents immediate dumps
  • Gives project time to develop before team can sell

Red Flags:

  • No cliff for team/advisor tokens (can dump immediately)
  • Short cliff for large allocations (3 months or less)
  • Cliff only for public sale, not for team (unfair distribution)

Ideal Structure:

  • Team/Advisors: 12-month cliff, 24-36 month vesting
  • Investors: 6-12 month cliff, 12-24 month vesting
  • Public sale: Partial unlock at TGE (10-20%), rest over 3-12 months

linear_vesting.title: Linear Vesting Schedules
linear_vesting.content:
Linear vesting releases tokens in equal amounts over a period. Most common and straightforward method.

Example:

  • Total allocation: 100,000 tokens
  • Vesting: 12 months linear after 6-month cliff
  • Month 6 (cliff ends): 8,333 tokens unlock
  • Months 7-18: 8,333 tokens unlock each month

Calculating Price Pressure:

If you know the vesting schedule, you can predict token unlock events:

  • Total supply: 100M tokens
  • Team allocation: 20M (20%)
  • Vesting: 12-month cliff, 24-month linear
  • Monthly unlock after cliff: 20M / 24 = 833,333 tokens per month

If the project has $10M market cap at cliff end, and 833k tokens unlock monthly:

  • At current price, that's ~$100k of potential sell pressure monthly
  • If team sells aggressively, this is bearish
  • If team holds, bullish signal

Smart investors: Track unlock schedules and adjust positions accordingly. Major unlocks often trigger price drops.

unlock_schedules.title: Analyzing Unlock Schedules
unlock_schedules.content:
Key Questions to Ask:

  1. What percentage unlocks at TGE? (Token Generation Event)
    • Ideal: 5-15% for initial liquidity
    • Red flag: 50%+ (massive dump risk)
  2. When do team tokens unlock?
    • Ideal: 12+ month cliff
    • Red flag: No cliff or short cliff
  3. What's the total vesting duration?
    • Ideal: 24-48 months
    • Red flag: Less than 12 months
  4. Are there any "unlock cliffs" (big one-time releases)?
    • Watch for dates when large amounts unlock simultaneously

Example Analysis: Project XYZ

  • Total Supply: 1 billion tokens
  • TGE Unlock: 10% (100M tokens)
  • Team: 20% (200M), 12-month cliff, 36-month linear
  • Investors: 30% (300M), 6-month cliff, 18-month linear
  • Public: 10% (100M), 20% at TGE, 12-month linear

Projected Unlock Timeline:

  • Month 0 (TGE): 120M tokens circulating (12%)
  • Month 6: Investor cliff ends—major sell pressure begins
  • Month 12: Team cliff ends—more sell pressure
  • Month 24: Investor vesting complete—stabilization
  • Month 48: All vesting complete

Trading Strategy:

  • Buy at launch if good project, but expect dumps at month 6 and 12
  • Consider selling before major unlock dates
  • Re-accumulate after unlock sell pressure passes
  • Long-term hold only if fundamentals justify the dilution

evaluation_criteria.title: Evaluating Launch Opportunities
evaluation_criteria.content: With thousands of launches annually and a high failure rate, rigorous evaluation is essential. Here's a framework for due diligence.

team.title: Team Assessment
team.content:
What to Research:

  1. Public Identities: Are team members fully doxxed with real names, photos, and LinkedIn profiles?
    • Red flag: Anonymous team for non-privacy focused projects
  2. Track Record: What have they built before?
    • Look for: Previous successful exits, relevant experience
    • Red flag: First-time founders with no relevant background
  3. Technical Expertise: Can they execute the roadmap?
    • Check GitHub activity, technical whitepapers, code quality
    • Red flag: No technical co-founder, no GitHub activity
  4. Advisors: Who's backing them?
    • Good sign: Reputable advisors actively involved
    • Red flag: Paid advisors with no real involvement

How to Research:

  • LinkedIn: Verify employment history
  • Twitter/X: Check activity, engagement, reputation
  • GitHub: Review code contributions
  • Google: Search for any controversies or past failures
  • Community: Ask in project Discord—serious teams engage

Example: Good Team

  • Founder: Previously led engineering at Coinbase
  • CTO: Core contributor to Ethereum for 5 years
  • Advisors: Vitalik Buterin (actively engaged), Naval Ravikant
  • GitHub: Active development, 50+ contributors

Example: Red Flags

  • Founder: No LinkedIn, anonymous
  • Team: Stock photos or AI-generated images
  • Advisors: Just logos with no confirmation of involvement
  • GitHub: Forked project with no original code

tokenomics.title: Tokenomics Analysis
tokenomics.content:
Supply Distribution: How are tokens allocated?

Healthy Distribution:

  • Community/Ecosystem: 40-60%
  • Team/Advisors: 10-20%
  • Investors: 10-25%
  • Treasury/Foundation: 10-20%
  • Public Sale: 5-15%

Red Flag Distribution:

  • Team + Investors > 50% (majority controlled by insiders)
  • Public sale < 3% (not enough decentralization)
  • Unclear allocations or "Other" category > 10%

Utility Analysis: What does the token do?

  • Good utility:
    • Governance (vote on protocol changes)
    • Revenue share (fee distribution to holders)
    • Staking rewards (incentivize holding)
    • Required for platform use (transaction fees, access)
  • Weak utility:
    • "Governance" with no real power
    • Staking with unsustainable yields
    • No clear reason to hold long-term

Emission Schedule: How fast do new tokens enter circulation?

  • High inflation (10%+ per year): Constant sell pressure
  • Moderate inflation (2-5%): Reasonable if matched by growth
  • Deflationary (burns): Bullish if sustainable

Market Cap Evaluation:

  • FDV (Fully Diluted Valuation): Market cap if all tokens were circulating
  • Circulating Market Cap: Current circulating supply × price
  • Red flag: FDV > 10x circulating market cap (huge dilution ahead)

Example Comparison:

  • Project A: $10M market cap, $500M FDV (50x dilution—avoid)
  • Project B: $10M market cap, $30M FDV (3x dilution—reasonable)

product.title: Product and Market Fit
product.content:
Product Stage Assessment:

  1. Idea Stage: Just a whitepaper, no working product
    • Risk: Extremely high (90%+ fail to deliver)
    • Only invest if team is exceptional and you're okay losing it all
  2. MVP/Beta: Working prototype, limited functionality
    • Risk: High (50%+ fail to gain traction)
    • Look for: User feedback, iteration speed, clear roadmap
  3. Live Product: Fully functional, has real users
    • Risk: Moderate (depends on competition and growth)
    • Look for: User growth, revenue, retention metrics
  4. Established Product: Proven market fit, significant users/revenue
    • Risk: Lower, but growth may be priced in
    • Look for: Moat, network effects, expansion plans

Traction Metrics:

  • Users: How many? Growing or stagnant?
  • Revenue: Any? Growing? Sustainable model?
  • Activity: Daily transactions, volume, engagement
  • Retention: Do users come back?

Competitive Analysis:

  • Who are the competitors?
  • What's the differentiation?
  • Is there a clear moat (network effect, technology, community)?
  • Can they actually compete with established players?

Market Size:

  • Is the problem big enough to justify the valuation?
  • Total Addressable Market (TAM) analysis
  • Is crypto necessary for this solution?

Red Flags:

  • No working product at launch
  • Copying existing projects with no innovation
  • Overpromising ("Ethereum killer", "10,000x potential")
  • No clear go-to-market strategy
  • Token sale to fund development of an idea (not execution)

risks_scams.title: Risks and Common Scams
risks_scams.content: The token launch space is filled with scams and failed projects. Estimated 80%+ of launches fail or are outright scams. Here's how to protect yourself.

rug_pulls.title: Understanding Rug Pulls
rug_pulls.content:
What is a Rug Pull? When developers abandon a project and take investors' money, often by removing liquidity or dumping pre-allocated tokens.

Types of Rug Pulls:

  1. Liquidity Removal:
    • Dev adds liquidity to DEX, waits for hype
    • Removes all liquidity, leaving token worthless
    • Prevention: Check if liquidity is locked (via services like Team Finance)
  2. Token Dump:
    • Team holds massive allocation
    • Dumps on unsuspecting buyers
    • Prevention: Check token distribution and vesting
  3. Smart Contract Backdoor:
    • Contract has hidden functions to mint unlimited tokens or freeze trading
    • Prevention: Smart contract audit, check for verified contracts
  4. Slow Rug:
    • Team gradually sells allocation over time
    • Development slows, promises unkept
    • Prevention: Monitor GitHub activity and roadmap delivery

Famous Rug Pulls:

  • Squid Game Token (SQUID): Nov 2021, $3M+ stolen. Contract had code preventing selling, only devs could sell.
  • AnubisDAO: Oct 2021, $60M stolen in minutes after launch. Liquidity immediately drained.
  • Meerkat Finance: Mar 2021, $31M rug pull on BSC. Vault code had hidden withdrawal function.

red_flags.title: Red Flags Checklist
red_flags.content:
Team Red Flags:

  • ❌ Anonymous team for non-privacy projects
  • ❌ Stock photos or fake identities
  • ❌ No LinkedIn or verifiable history
  • ❌ Previous failed projects not disclosed
  • ❌ Overly aggressive marketing ("guaranteed 100x")

Tokenomics Red Flags:

  • ❌ Team allocation > 30%
  • ❌ No vesting or short vesting for team
  • ❌ Unclear token distribution
  • ❌ Mint function in contract (can create infinite tokens)
  • ❌ Pause function allowing dev to freeze trading

Product Red Flags:

  • ❌ No working product, just promises
  • ❌ Copied whitepaper (plagiarism)
  • ❌ Unrealistic roadmap ("We'll replace Ethereum")
  • ❌ No GitHub activity or closed source
  • ❌ No clear use case for the token

Launch Red Flags:

  • ❌ No liquidity lock
  • ❌ Unaudited smart contracts
  • ❌ Liquidity provided entirely by the team
  • ❌ Suspiciously high APY (Ponzinomics)
  • ❌ Requires recruiting others (pyramid scheme)

Community Red Flags:

  • ❌ Fake Twitter followers (sudden jumps, low engagement)
  • ❌ Telegram/Discord with only hype, no substance
  • ❌ Mods delete critical questions
  • ❌ Pressure to buy ("Last chance!", "FOMO now!")

If you spot 3+ red flags, walk away. If you spot 5+, it's definitely a scam.

due_diligence.title: Due Diligence Process
due_diligence.content:
Step-by-Step Checklist:

  1. Team Research (15-30 min):
    • Google each team member
    • Check LinkedIn profiles
    • Review GitHub activity
    • Search for past controversies
  2. Smart Contract Audit (10 min):
    • Is it audited by reputable firm? (CertiK, Trail of Bits, OpenZeppelin)
    • Read the audit report—were critical issues found and fixed?
    • Check contract on Etherscan/BSCscan—is it verified?
    • Use tools like Token Sniffer to check for common scam patterns
  3. Tokenomics Review (15 min):
    • Read token distribution breakdown
    • Check vesting schedules on the website or whitepaper
    • Calculate FDV vs market cap
    • Look for liquidity lock proof
  4. Product Testing (20-30 min):
    • Use the product if it exists
    • Check GitHub for real development
    • Search for competitors
    • Read the whitepaper (technical sections, not just marketing)
  5. Community Assessment (10 min):
    • Join Discord/Telegram
    • Ask critical questions—how do they respond?
    • Check Twitter engagement (real or bot followers?)
    • Read Reddit threads for unbiased opinions
  6. Comparable Analysis (10 min):
    • What's the market cap of similar projects?
    • Is the valuation reasonable?
    • What's the competitive advantage?

Total time: 1-2 hours per project. If you can't spend this time, you shouldn't invest.

Tools for Due Diligence:

  • Token Sniffer: Scam detection
  • RugDoc: Security reviews
  • DexTools: Chart analysis and holder distribution
  • Etherscan/BSCscan: Contract verification
  • CoinGecko/CMC: Market data and links

post_launch_strategies.title: Post-Launch Trading Strategies
post_launch_strategies.content: The launch is just the beginning. Smart participants have strategies for when to sell, when to hold, and how to manage risk.

timing.title: When to Sell
timing.content:
Common Selling Strategies:

  1. Immediate Flip (High Risk):
    • Sell immediately at launch for quick profit
    • Works if: Launch is massively oversubscribed and hype is high
    • Risks: May sell too early, price can 10x from launch
  2. Take Initial Investment Out:
    • Wait for 2-3x, sell enough to recover initial investment
    • Let the rest ride for free
    • Works if: You want to eliminate downside risk
  3. Ladder Out:
    • Sell in increments (25% at 2x, 25% at 5x, 25% at 10x, hold 25%)
    • Works if: You believe in long-term potential but want to lock profits
  4. Hold for Milestones:
    • Set specific targets (product launch, exchange listing, mainnet)
    • Sell portion at each milestone
    • Works if: You're following the roadmap closely

Market Cycle Considerations:

  • Bull Market: Can hold longer, prices often continue rising
  • Bear Market: Take profits faster, rallies are usually short-lived
  • Sideways: Sell into strength, buy dips

Unlock Events:

  • Major unlocks typically cause 10-30% price drops
  • Consider selling 1-2 weeks before major unlocks
  • Re-buy after sell pressure subsides if you're bullish long-term

Psychology:

  • Don't get emotionally attached—tokens are not your identity
  • Taking profits is not "betraying" the project
  • Better to sell too early and miss gains than hold too long and lose everything

monitoring.title: Monitoring Your Investments
monitoring.content:
What to Track:

  1. Development Progress:
    • GitHub activity—are devs still coding?
    • Roadmap milestones—are they being hit?
    • Product updates—is there real progress?
  2. Token Metrics:
    • Price and market cap trends
    • Trading volume (declining volume = fading interest)
    • Holder distribution (whales accumulating or dumping?)
  3. Community Health:
    • Discord/Telegram activity—growing or dying?
    • Twitter engagement—real or bot followers?
    • Team communication—frequent and transparent?
  4. Partnerships and Integration:
    • New exchange listings
    • Protocol integrations
    • Strategic partnerships announced
  5. Competitor Activity:
    • Are competitors shipping faster?
    • Are they gaining market share?
    • Is your project falling behind?

Tools for Monitoring:

  • DexTools/DexScreener: Price charts, holder analytics
  • Nansen: Whale tracking (who's buying/selling?)
  • Lunar Crush: Social sentiment analysis
  • GitHub: Code commits and contributor activity
  • Google Alerts: News mentions

Warning Signs to Sell:

  • Development stops (no GitHub commits for weeks)
  • Team goes silent (no updates)
  • Roadmap repeatedly delayed
  • Key team members leave
  • Community complains about unkept promises
  • Trading volume dries up

portfolio_management.title: Portfolio Management
portfolio_management.content:
Position Sizing:

  • High Risk (Idea stage): 1-3% of portfolio max
  • Medium Risk (Beta product): 3-8% of portfolio
  • Lower Risk (Live product, proven traction): 5-15% of portfolio
  • Never: Go all-in on a single launch, no matter how good it looks

Diversification Across Launches:

  • Don't put all funds into one launch cycle
  • Spread across multiple launches (some will fail, some will 10x)
  • Diversify across launchpads (different platforms, different vetting)
  • Diversify across sectors (DeFi, GameFi, Infra, etc.)

Example Portfolio Allocation:

  • 40%: Blue-chip crypto (ETH, BTC)
  • 30%: Established mid-caps
  • 20%: Recent launches with traction
  • 10%: New launches (spread across 5-10 projects)

Rebalancing:

  • If a launch does 10x, it now represents a huge portion of your portfolio
  • Rebalance by taking profits, keep position size reasonable
  • Reinvest profits into new opportunities or stables

Tax Considerations:

  • Short-term gains taxed higher than long-term (in many countries)
  • Track cost basis for all purchases
  • Consider tax-loss harvesting (sell losers to offset gains)
  • Consult a crypto tax specialist—this gets complicated

Mental Stops:

  • Decide in advance: "If this drops 50%, I'll sell"
  • Or: "If it doesn't hit X milestone by Y date, I'll exit"
  • Don't let hope override your strategy
  • Emotional holding is how people ride tokens to zero

Continuous Learning:

  • Review past investments—what worked, what didn't?
  • Keep a journal of your decisions and outcomes
  • Learn from mistakes without beating yourself up
  • Stay humble—this market humbles everyone eventually

ido.definition: A token launch that occurs directly on a decentralized exchange, providing immediate liquidity and trading. Unlike ICOs which required waiting for exchange listings, IDOs allow instant price discovery and trading.

ieo.definition: A token sale conducted on a centralized exchange platform (like Binance Launchpad). The exchange vets the project, handles the sale, and provides immediate listing. Generally considered safer than ICOs due to exchange due diligence.

ico.definition: The original token sale method, popular in 2017. Projects accepted cryptocurrency (usually ETH) directly in exchange for tokens. Now largely replaced by IDOs and IEOs due to regulatory concerns and high scam rates.

fair_launch.definition: A token launch with no presale, no team allocation at launch, and equal access for all participants. The philosophy is that even the team must buy or earn tokens like everyone else, preventing insider advantages and early dumps.

lbp.definition: A type of token launch using dynamic pricing that starts high and gradually decreases. This discourages bots and FOMO buying, allowing for better price discovery. The declining price curve continues until market demand stabilizes the price.

allocation.definition: The amount of tokens you're permitted to purchase in a launch. Can be guaranteed (fixed amount), lottery-based (random selection), or determined by tier (based on platform token holdings).

vesting.definition: A schedule that determines when and how tokens are released over time. Vesting prevents immediate dumps by locking tokens and releasing them gradually, aligning long-term incentives for teams and early investors.

cliff.definition: An initial lockup period in a vesting schedule where zero tokens are released. After the cliff period ends, vesting begins. For example, a "12-month cliff" means no tokens unlock for the first year.

tge.definition: The moment when a token is created and first becomes available. This is typically when the initial circulating supply enters the market and trading begins. Often used interchangeably with "launch" or "listing."

whitelist.definition: A pre-approved list of wallet addresses permitted to participate in a token launch. Getting whitelisted usually requires completing tasks (KYC, social media follows, holding platform tokens) or winning a lottery.
